contract.goal: An API-compatibility gate over every published library, a computed version that tells the gate what a build is allowed to break, and the deprecation, changelog and artifact-set rules that make both meaningful.
contract.output: revapi + semver extension in the reactor root (inert until the baseline is published); maven-javadoc-plugin pinned and attached under -Pci; maven-jar-plugin pinned; requirePluginVersions in the root POM and in ludwig-service-parent; Checkstyle MissingDeprecated + DeprecationWithoutSince; CHANGELOG.md/.ru.md with a -Prelease enforcer rule; gitversion.yml + a Jenkinsfile version stage; scripts/check_image_pins.sh wired into scripts/gate.sh; docs updated.
constraints: No new in-repo dependency: every addition is a build plugin, so the reactor DAG is unchanged
revapi reaches the 25 jar libraries by being declared in the reactor root, and must never reach the two services
ludwig-bom is not touched: it holds third-party dependency versions, not plugin configuration
No relaxation to make a build pass: no weakened Checkstyle or ArchUnit rule, no disabled test, no revapi severity lowered to hide a real difference
The gate lands inert (failBuildOnProblemsFound off); arming it requires a published 1.1.0 baseline, which is an operator step an agent may not perform (-Pci and deploy are denied)
-Drevapi.skip=true is a command-line hatch only and must not appear in any POM, script or Jenkinsfile
Doclint fails on malformed Javadoc only; the 288 missing-Javadoc warnings stay warnings

decisions: 1.2: requirePluginVersions reported four plugins bound from Maven 3.9.16's super-POM (maven-clean-plugin 3.2.0, maven-install-plugin 3.1.4, maven-deploy-plugin 3.1.4, maven-site-plugin 3.12.1) and then maven-resources-plugin 3.4.0 for the jar modules. Pinned all five in the reactor root's pluginManagement at exactly the versions Maven binds today rather than naming them in <unCheckedPluginList>. Pinning is the same amount of text, changes no behaviour, and leaves the exclusion list empty; excluding them would have left the installation deciding the version of `install` and `deploy`. ludwig-service-parent needed only maven-site-plugin, because spring-boot-starter-parent already pins the rest.
1.2: no unCheckedPluginList and no grep fallback were needed. `mvn -q validate` exits 0 across the whole reactor.

2.2: DeprecationWithoutSince is `@Deprecated(?!\s*\((?=[^)]*\bsince\s*=)(?=[^)]*\bforRemoval\s*=))` - two lookaheads anchored inside one argument list by [^)]*, so a second annotation on the same line cannot lend its members to the first. Two limits are written beside the rule: RegexpSinglelineJava sees one line, so a split annotation is invisible (acceptable because formatting mirrors IntelliJ's defaults, which keep members on the declaration line), and it has no notion of a string literal, so a source file that writes the annotation's name inside a string trips it - which is why DeprecationContractRulesTest spells its expected message without the leading at-sign. That second limit was found by the rule failing the build on the test's own constant, not reasoned about in advance.

2.3: the six existing @Deprecated sites (all in odata-filter-spring-boot-starter) got `forRemoval = false`, not `true`. The rule demands that the answer be explicit, not that it be a particular answer, and declaring `forRemoval = true` would commit the platform to removing the ODataQuery argument resolver - a product decision outside this change. Under the api-evolution capability that also means the resolver cannot be removed until some release first publishes it with forRemoval = true, which is the process working.

2.2: checkstyle-rules gained src/test for the first time. The three test dependencies are test-scoped, so the 'must not drag anything onto a consumer's classpath' constraint in its POM still holds; the checkstyle engine is pinned to ${checkstyle.version}, the same number the maven-checkstyle-plugin's dependency override uses, so the test runs on the engine the build runs. The deliberately non-compliant fixtures live under src/test/resources, which the plugin's sourceDirectories exclude - putting them in src/test/java would fail the build they exist to test. The module's `<skip>true</skip>` on maven-checkstyle-plugin was removed, because it now has Java to check.

4.2: the evaluateBeanshell conditions read the files with `new java.util.Scanner(new java.io.File(...), "UTF-8").useDelimiter("\\A").next()`, not with java.nio.file.Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(...)). The nio form fails at runtime with `Couldn't evaluate condition` - BeanShell 2.0 has no varargs, so it cannot resolve Paths.get(String, String...). Each condition is a single expression for the same reason: BeanShell returns the value of an expression, and a multi-statement script is not reliably a Boolean.

5.2: the plugin CANNOT distinguish an absent baseline from an unresolvable one - both surface as `Failed to resolve old artifacts` and failOnUnresolvedArtifacts fails on both or neither. Real output with nothing published: `[WARNING] Failed to resolve old artifacts: Failed to find a version of artifact 'ru.ludwigandreas:jira-client:jar:RELEASE' that would correspond to an expression '^.*(?<!-SNAPSHOT)$'. The versions found were: []. The API analysis will proceed comparing the new archives against an empty archive.` So scripts/check_api_baseline.sh makes the distinction outside the build, using GIT TAGS as the record of what has been released - which is sound precisely because this change makes a release a tag. No tag means no release means every baseline is legitimately absent; a tag means each module that existed at that tag must have a resolvable jar. Both branches were run: with no tag it exits 0 and says the check is absent rather than passing; with a temporary local v1.0.0-tmptest tag and LUDWIG_REPO_RELEASES_URL pointed at an unreachable host it exits 1 and names all 25 modules. 4.2 FOLLOW-UP, after the user ran `mvn -Prelease` with no -Drevision and got three errors for one mistake: both changelog conditions now short-circuit on `"${project.version}".endsWith("-SNAPSHOT")`. Without it the version stays at the .mvn/maven.config fallback and the two rules demand a `## [1.1.0-SNAPSHOT]` heading, telling the reader to write a changelog entry for a version that can never be released - while requireReleaseVersion, two lines above, already says the right thing. The rule is not weakened: a SNAPSHOT never reaches the releases repository, so there is no pinnable version the short-circuit lets through. The three messages were also collapsed onto one line each; the XML indentation of a wrapped <message> is reproduced verbatim in the output.

POST-HANDOFF 1: `mvn clean install` failed with `No enum constant SeverityLevel.WARNING PACKAGE.INFO.SEVERITY=IGNORE`. Cause was NOT a rule: the root pom.xml had been reformatted (~800 lines re-indented) and the formatter joined <propertyExpansion>'s two lines into one. maven-checkstyle-plugin feeds that string to java.util.Properties.load, which is line-oriented, so it read ONE key whose value was 'warning package.info.severity=ignore'. Whitespace there is semantic. Both occurrences (root POM and ludwig-service-parent, the second not yet reformatted but identically fragile) now use 
, which a formatter cannot collapse and the XML parser turns back into a newline, with a comment at each site saying not to tidy it back.

POST-HANDOFF 2: with failBuildOnProblemsFound armed and NO baseline published, three successive builds went red, none for a compatibility reason - which is precisely what acceptance step 8.3 was for, arriving early. java.class.externalClassExposedInAPI (several hundred Spring types reached transitively from one @Bean returning LocalValidatorFactoryBean) and java.class.nonPublicPartOfAPI (WireMock and Testcontainers internals behind test-support's fixtures) are revapi's API-DESIGN advisory family: both are computed from the NEW archive alone, fire identically on a build with no source change, and would fire on a first release when there is nothing to be compatible with. Exempted together by one regex entry with a justification.

POST-HANDOFF 3: java.missing.newClass split into two cases that got DIFFERENT answers on purpose. jakarta.servlet.* in odata-filter was resolvable and merely unresolved - it arrives transitively at `provided` scope - so it was fixed at the cause with resolveTransitiveProvidedDependencies (not the plugin's default). revapi's own message says the analysis 'may be incorrect' without those classes, and ignoring a class it COULD have loaded turns an incorrect analysis into a quiet one. The 23 SAML2/LDAP/OAuth2-client types behind HttpSecurity.saml2Login()/ldapAuthentication()/oauth2Client() are not resolvable at all: they live in jars this platform does not depend on and must not start depending on to satisfy a checker. Those are exempted, and they can never be a difference because they are absent from both archives.

POST-HANDOFF 4: the standing rule for any future exemption, now written into docs/harness-enforcement.md - a code that compares TWO archives stays armed; a code computed from ONE archive is not a compatibility statement. java.method.removed, parameterTypeChanged, addedToInterface, field.removed, class.removed and kindChanged are all in the first group and all armed.

POST-HANDOFF 5: Docker was running this time, so the full build needed no exclusions at all. `mvn clean install` BUILD SUCCESS across all 31 reactor entries with the gate armed; revapi ran 28 times and reported zero problems; aggregate coverage is 72.3% instruction / 61.4% branch, against the 50.2%/48.9% measured earlier with the Testcontainers classes excluded - the gap was the integration tests, not a coverage change.
failures: 3.1/3.2 BLOCKED, and it blocks the operator step 8.2 as well. Four public methods in two modules declare a Lombok-@Builder-generated type as their RETURN type - export-spring-boot-starter's ReportDefinition.of -> ReportDefinitionBuilder, Column.of -> ColumnBuilder, EnrichmentStage.of -> EnrichmentStageBuilder, and user-settings-spring-boot-starter's SettingDefinition.of -> SettingDefinitionBuilder. Lombok generates those types into bytecode and never into source, so javadoc cannot resolve them and fails with `cannot find symbol`, which is a javac error and not a doclint category - no doclint group, and nothing short of <failOnError>false</failOnError>, silences it. Three fixes were tried and measured: (1) -processorpath + -proc:full on the javadoc tool - refused, `error: invalid flag: -processorpath`, javadoc runs no annotation processors; (2) appending a second --class-path - javadoc takes the last one and every other import then fails; (3) prepending target/classes to the single -classpath - still fails, because the class's own source is on the sourcepath and javac prefers source over class, and the nested builder is not in that source. The only remaining mechanism is a delombok step, which design.md Goals/Non-Goals rules out. The conflict is real and belongs to the artifacts: published-artifact-set REQUIRES a -javadoc jar for every jar module, and without delombok two of the 25 cannot produce one. RESOLVED: the user chose to amend design.md and add delombok in the `ci` profile. lombok-maven-plugin 1.18.20.0 with its bundled Lombok overridden to 1.18.38, `delombok` bound to generate-sources inside -Pci, addOutputDirectory=false so nothing compiles from the copy, and maven-javadoc-plugin sourcepath = generated-sources/delombok + generated-sources/annotations. Verified: `mvn -DskipTests -fae package org.projectlombok:lombok-maven-plugin:1.18.20.0:delombok javadoc:jar` produces a -javadoc jar for all 24 library modules that have Java, and zero javadoc errors. checkstyle-rules produces none because it has no main sources, and the two services produce none, which is what the spec requires.
